rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قضى is a decisive command; أن explains it, with ألا تعبدوا functioning as a prohibition. باء cannot attach to إحسانا because a verbal noun cannot precede its complement.
rows.anchor: وأمر أمرا مقطوعا به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Variant readings are وأوصى, وصى from Ibn ʿAbbās, and وقضاء ربك from a descendant of Muʿādh ibn Jabal.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وأوصى ) وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إما adds ما to إن for emphasis and permits the emphatic nūn; أحدهما is the subject of يبلغن, while the dual reading makes it replace the pronoun. كلاهما is a بدل, not emphasis, because أو presents alternatives.
rows.anchor: هي ( إن ) الشرطية زيدت عليها ( ما ) تأكيدا لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أف is a sound of irritation, read with three vowel patterns, with or without tanwīn, explained through its original form and Arabic analogies.
rows.anchor: صوت يدل على تضجر . وقرىء : ( أف )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عندك depicts parents grown old and helpless, dependent in their child's home; the child must be patient and gentle despite this difficult burden.
rows.anchor: هو أن يكبرا ويعجزا ، وكانا كلا على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The injunction is emphatic because filial kindness is paired with God's unity; even slight irritation is forbidden, and ولا تنهرهما bars rebuking them.
rows.anchor: ولقد بالغ سبحانه في التوصية بهما حيث افتتحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قولا كريما means beautiful, courteous speech; one view specifies يا أبتاه and يا أماه and forbids calling parents by name as rude, though this is allowed when they are absent.
rows.anchor: بدل التأفيف والنهر { قولا كريما } جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: جناح الذل/الذل is read with two vowels and explained either as a humbled or docile wing, or as giving humility toward parents a low wing; both intensify submission.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن يكون المعنى : واخفض لهما جناحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الرحمة means abundant compassion for parents dependent on a child who once depended on them; pray for lasting mercy in return for childhood care. For unbelieving parents, pray conditionally for guidance; some say such prayers were abrogated.
rows.anchor: من فرط رحمتك لهما وعطفك عليهما ، لكبرهما

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUyayna says charity for the dead reaches them, but seeking forgiveness benefits them most; if anything were better, God would have prescribed it for parents.
rows.anchor: وسئل ابن عيينة ، عن الصدقة عن الميت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report says God's approval rests on parents' approval and His anger on their anger.
rows.anchor: رضا الله في رضا الوالدين ، وسخطه في سخطهما

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report contrasts the dutiful person's safety from Hell with the disobedient person's exclusion from Paradise.
rows.anchor: يفعل البار ما يشاء أن يفعل فلن يدخل النار

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says a dutiful child does not die an evil death.
rows.anchor: وروي سعيد بن المسيب : إن البار لا يموت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A man asks whether tending aged parents repays their care in his childhood; the Prophet says no, since they wanted him to live while he wants them to die.
rows.anchor: إن أبوي بلغا من الكبر أني ألي منهما ماوليا مني في الصغر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A father explains that he once supported the son who now withholds his wealth; the Prophet weeps and says the son and his wealth belong to his father.
rows.anchor: فبكى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وقال : ما من حجر ولا مدر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Pregnancy, nursing, and a mother's sleepless care cannot be repaid even by carrying her on pilgrimage; even one labor pain remains unpaid.
rows.anchor: وشكا إليه آخر سوء خلق أمه فقال : لم تكن

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar sees a man carrying his mother during circumambulation and says even one groan would remain unpaid; the man recites a poem about carrying her.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر أنه رأى رجلا في الطواف يحمل أمه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic warning says the disobedient, severer of kinship, elderly adulterer, and arrogant wearer of a trailing garment will not smell Paradise from a thousand years' distance.
rows.anchor: وعنه عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( 612 ) ( إياكم وعقوق الوالدين

rows.speaker: الفقهاء
rows.claim: Jurists say not to take one's father to church, but to fetch him if summoned; do not hand him wine, and take away the vessel after he drinks.
rows.anchor: وقال الفقهاء : لا يذهب بأبيه إلى البيعة

rows.speaker: أبو يوسف
rows.claim: Abū Yūsuf permits a son to light a fire under a parent's pot even when it contains pork.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي يوسف : إذا أمره أن يوقد تحت قدره

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Ḥudhayfa asks the Prophet for permission to kill his father among the polytheists; the Prophet says to leave the killing to someone else.
rows.anchor:
وعن حذيفة
( 613 ) أنه استأذن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الفضيل بن عياض
rows.claim: Al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ says honoring parents means not serving them lazily; another view forbids raising one's voice or glaring, calls for compassion and prayer, and serving their friends.
rows.anchor: وسئل الفضيل بن عياض عن بر الوالدين فقال : أن لا تقوم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report calls maintaining ties with one's father's friends among the best forms of filial devotion.
rows.anchor: فعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم . ( 614 ) ( إن من أبر البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the intention to honor parents; when righteous people lapse in anger, distress, or religious zeal and repent, God forgives them.
rows.anchor: بما في ضمائركم من قصد البر إلى الوالدين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explains the verse as covering an impulsive act toward one's father meant only for good.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : هي في البادرة تكون من

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib defines an awwāb as one who hastens to repent whenever he sins; the author also allows a general sense including a repentant child who wronged a parent.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن المسيب : الأواب الرجل كلما أذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥanīfa requires a wealthy person to support poor, unable-to-earn unmarriageable relatives; al-Shāfiʿī limits support to parents and children. Wealthy or non-maḥram kin are owed visits, affection, good companionship, and mutual aid.
rows.anchor: وحقهم إذا كانوا محارم كالأبوين والولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor and traveler receive zakāt, indicating that relatives' due is financial care; some say ذي القربى means the Messenger's relatives.
rows.anchor: { والمساكين وابن السبيل } يعني وآت هؤلاء حقهم من الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabdhīr is spending where wealth does not belong. Pre-Islamic Arabs squandered it for boasting; God directs spending to proper acts that bring one near Him.
rows.anchor: التبذير تفريق المال فيما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh defines waste as spending wealth outside its rightful due; Mujāhid says even a mudd spent on falsehood is waste.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله : هو إنفاق المال في غير حقه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: When one person says there is no good in extravagance, another replies that good works have no extravagance.
rows.anchor: فقال له صاحبه : لا خير في السرف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet rebukes Saʿd's excessive ablution, even if he washes beside a flowing river.
rows.anchor: وعن عبد الله بن عمرو . ( 615 ) مر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بسعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasteful people are like Satan in wickedness, his obedient friends, or his companions in Hell; Satan is ungrateful and must not be obeyed. Al-Ḥasan reads إخوان الشيطان in the singular.
rows.anchor: أمثالهم في الشرارة وهي غاية المذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image censures withholding and extravagant giving, commanding moderation. The extravagant person is blamed by God, people, and himself; محسورا means exhausted and left with nothing.
rows.anchor: هذا تمثيل لمنع الشحيح وإعطاء المسرف ، وأمر بالاقتصاد

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports that a child asks the Prophet for his shirt for his mother; the Prophet gives it away, stays shirtless, and misses the call to prayer.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر : ( 617 ) بينا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جالس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after giving al-Aqraʿ and ʿUyayna one hundred camels each, the Prophet gave ʿAbbās ibn Mirdās another hundred after his complaint and poem; revelation followed.
rows.anchor: وقيل ( 618 ) أعطى الأقرع بن حابس مائة من الإبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricted provision does not signal low standing or stinginess; God's apportionment follows wisdom. Another view says God holds the treasuries, while people must moderate their spending.
rows.anchor: بأن ذلك ليس لهوان منك عليه ، ولا لبخل به عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands or restricts provision at a middle course: neither the fullest desire nor the worst hardship is granted; people should follow this pattern.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أنه عز وعلا بسط لعباده أو قبض ، فإنه يراعي أوسط الحالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children were killed by burying daughters alive from fear of poverty; God forbids it and guarantees provision. Readings vary in خشية and خطأ, which can mean sin or error.
rows.anchor: قتلهم أولادهم : هو وأدهم بناتهم ، كانوا يئدونهن خشية الفاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fāḥisha means exceptionally vile; adultery is a wretched path violating another's spouse or close female relative without lawful marriage.
rows.anchor: قبيحة زائدة على حد القبح { وساء سبيلا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protected life may be taken only for disbelief, deliberate murder, or adultery after marriage; مظلوما means the victim committed none of these. His walī is an entitled relative or the ruler; sulṭān means authority or proof to claim retaliation.
rows.anchor: إلا بإحدى ثلاث : إلا بأن تكفر ، أو تقتل مؤمنا عمدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فلا يسرف forbids the walī to kill anyone beyond the murderer or several people for one victim, as in pre-Islamic vendetta; another view means no mutilation.
rows.anchor: فلا يقتل غير القاتل ، ولا اثنين والقاتل واحد

rows.speaker: أبو مسلم صاحب الدولة
rows.claim: Abū Muslim reads يسرف in the indicative, a declarative form with an especially forceful command.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو مسلم صاحب الدولة : ( فلا يسرف )

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid takes the pronoun in فلا يسرف to refer to the original killer; other readings address the walī or killer directly, and Ubayy has the plural prohibition.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد : أن الضمير للقاتل الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: منصور may mean the walī, already aided by law and ruler; the victim, aided by reward; or the killer wrongly slain by an excessive walī, since retaliation is prescribed for the aggressor.
rows.anchor: الضمير إما للولي ، يعني حسبه أن الله قد نصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: التي هي أحسن is the best course, preserving and investing the orphan's property; the covenant must be fulfilled, or is personified and questioned for breach, or its keeper is held responsible.
rows.anchor: بالخصلة أو الطريقة التي هي أحسن ، وهي حفظه عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qirṭās is read with ḍamma or kasra; it can mean a Roman balance or any scale. أحسن تأويلا means the best outcome, from āla, to return.
rows.anchor: وقرىء ( بالقسطاس ) بالضم والكسر ، وهو القرسطون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ولا تقف means do not follow, from tracking footsteps; it forbids following or saying and doing what one does not know, including blind imitation. Hearing, sight, and heart are each accountable.
rows.anchor: ولا تتبع . وقرىء ( ولا تقف ) . يقال : قفا أثره وقافه

rows.speaker: ابن الحنفية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya interprets it as forbidding false testimony; al-Ḥasan applies it to falsely claiming one saw or heard a Muslim do something.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن الحنفية : شهادة الزور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report threatens one who falsely imputes a trait to a believer with confinement in khabāl until he can justify himself; poetry uses the root for mutual accusation.
rows.anchor: من قفى مؤمنا بما ليس فيه حبسه الله في ردغة الخبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects using the verse to invalidate ijtihād: a preponderant judgment is knowledge recognized by law for action.
rows.anchor: وقد استدل به مبطل الاجتهاد ولم يصح ؛ لأن ذلك نوع من العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أولئك points to hearing, sight, and heart; عنه مسؤولا makes each the thing asked about. A reading opens the first vowels of فؤاد by changing hamza into wāw.
rows.anchor: في موضع الرفع بالفاعلية ، أي : كل واحد منها كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مرحا is a circumstantial accusative meaning arrogant; it is also read مرحا, and al-Akhfash favors the verbal noun for emphasis. Not piercing earth refers to futile trampling; a reading has ḍamma on rāʾ.
rows.anchor: حال ، أي : ذا مرح . وقرىء ( مرحا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the mountains in height mocks the arrogant person's pretension.
rows.anchor: بتطاولك . وهو تهكم بالمختال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word for evil has readings سيئة, سيئه, سيئا, and سيئات; Abū Bakr has كان شأنه. The author explains why the noun for sin need not agree in gender.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( سيئة ) و ( سيئه ) على إضافة سيء إلى ضمير كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because prior traits include good and bad, سيئة without genitive reference covers the prohibited traits alone; the possessive reading refers to the bad portion of the list.
rows.anchor: قلت : كل ذلك إحاطة بما نهى عنه خاصة لا بجميع الخصال المعدودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك refers to the passage from the command against associating another god in 17:22 through this point; it is wisdom because it is firmly composed and admits no corruption.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما تقدم من قوله { لا تجعل مع الله إلاها ءاخر }

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says these eighteen verses were on Moses' tablets; the Torah's Ten Commandments likewise begin and end with the ban on shirk, since tawḥīd is wisdom's foundation.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس : هذه الثماني عشرة آية كانت في ألواح موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without tawḥīd, wisdom and learning do not benefit even philosophers; the author says they are more astray than cattle.
rows.anchor: لأن التوحيد هو رأس كل حكمة وملاكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke asks whether God gave people the best children, sons, while taking inferior daughters for Himself, contrary to their values; the claim gives God bodily offspring and degrades the angels as female.
rows.anchor: أفخصكم ربكم على وجه الخلوص والصفاء بأفضل الأولاد وهم البنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They prefer themselves by assigning God what they dislike and lowering the angels, God's most noble creatures, by declaring them female.
rows.anchor: ثم بأنكم تفضلون عليه أنفسكم حيث تجعلون له ما تكرهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صرفنا في هذا القرآن may mean repeatedly refuting the claim that God has daughters, or repeating that argument with its object understood.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن يريد بهذا القرآن إبطال إضافتهم إلى الله البنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: صرفنا is read without shadda and ليذكروا with or without it; the repeated argument urges reflection and only increases opponents' aversion.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( صرفنا ) بالتخفيف وكذلك { ليذكروا } قرىء ( مشددا ومخففا )

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyān says the verse increased his humility as it increased the enemies' aversion.
rows.anchor: وعن سفيان : كان إذا قرأها قال : زادني لك خضوعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كما تقولون has tāʾ and yāʾ readings; rival gods would seek a way to the Lord of the Throne as kings compete for sovereignty. Another view is that they would seek nearness to Him, as in 17:57.
rows.anchor: قرىء ( كما تقولون ) بالتاء والياء . و { إذا } دالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument echoes the claim that multiple gods in heaven and earth would cause corruption.
rows.anchor: كما يفعل الملوك بعضهم مع بعض ، كقوله { لو كان فيهما الهة إلا الله }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: علوا means exaltation; calling it great intensifies God's disavowal of and distance from what they say.
rows.anchor: في معنى تعاليا . والمراد البراءة عن ذلك والنزاهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens, earth, and their contents glorify God through testimony of their state, demonstrating their Maker, power, and wisdom and declaring Him free of partners.
rows.anchor: والمراد أنها تسبح له بلسان الحال ، حيث تدل على الصانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address targets polytheists: associating partners while affirming God as Creator shows they failed to consider the evidence. Figurative glorification applies to all creation; otherwise a word would be literal and figurative at once.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للمشركين ، وهم وإن كانوا إذا سئلوا عن خالق السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's forbearance and forgiveness appear in delaying punishment despite heedlessness, bad reasoning, failure to understand the signs, and shirk.
rows.anchor: حين لا يعاجلكم بالعقوبة على غفلتكم وسوء نظركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حجابا مستورا may mean a veiling barrier, one invisible to sight, or one hidden behind other veils; the passage echoes the claim in 41:5 that hearts and ears are covered.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو حجاب لا يرى فهو مستور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن يفقهوه means preventing understanding; وحده is a verbal noun used adverbially for alone; نفورا is turning away or those who flee because they want idols mentioned with God.
rows.anchor: كراهة أن يفقهوه . أو لأن قوله { وجعلنا على قلوبهم أكنة }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Men from ʿAbd al-Dār disrupted recitation by clapping, whistling, and mixing poetry; the باء marks mocking manner, and إذ marks when they listened and whispered.
rows.anchor: كان يقوم عن يمينه إذا قرأ رجلان من عبد الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مسحورا can mean bewitched into madness, or derive from lung and mean a human like themselves.
rows.anchor: سحر فجن . وقيل : هو من السحر وهو الرئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They compare the Prophet to a poet, magician, or madman; having strayed among incompatible portrayals, they cannot find a way forward, like someone lost in a desert.
rows.anchor: مثلوك بالشاعر والساحر والمجنون { فضلوا } في جميع ذلك ضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response mirrors كنا with كونوا: God can restore bones, already part of the living body's framework, and even more lifeless stone or iron to life.
rows.anchor: لما قالوا : أئذاكنا عظاما قيل لهم { كونوا حجارة أو حديدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما يكبر في صدوركم is anything they consider too great to receive life; views identify it as death or the heavens and earth. سينغضون means shaking their heads toward the Prophet in mockery.
rows.anchor: يعني أو خلقا مما يكبر عندكم عن قبول الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling and responding are figurative: God raises them and they rise obediently; بحمده means they praise Him and hyperbolically depicts willing submission.
rows.anchor: والدعاء والاستجابة كلاهما مجاز . والمعنى : يوم يبعثكم فتنبعثون

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says they shake dust from their heads and declare God's glory and praise.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : ينفضون التراب عن رؤوسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The terror of resurrection makes them perceive their worldly stay as a day or part of one; Qatāda says the world seems insignificant once they see the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وترون الهول ، فعنده تستقصرون مدة لبثكم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should address polytheists gently, with the best phrase and without harshness, avoiding words that inflame them; one example is to say God may guide or show mercy to them.
rows.anchor: للمشركين الكلمة { التى هى أحسن } وألين ولا يخاشنوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's intervention sows corruption and quarrelling; the Prophet is not tasked with coercing people into Islam, so believers should be tolerant before the Sword verse.
rows.anchor: اعتراض ، يعني يلقي بينهم الفساد ويغري بعضهم على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say it was revealed about ʿUmar after an insult, or after Muslims complained of severe polytheist harassment.
rows.anchor: وقيل : نزلت في عمر رضي الله عنه : شتمه رجل

rows.speaker: طلحة
rows.claim: Ṭalḥa reads ينزغ with kasra; both vowel forms are dialect variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ طلحة : ( ينزغ ) بالكسر وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This rebuts Meccans who doubted Abū Ṭālib's orphan could be a prophet and poor followers such as Ṣuhayb, Bilāl, and Khabbāb could be chosen over their chiefs; God knows each person's merit.
rows.anchor: هو رد على أهل مكة في إنكارهم واستبعادهم أن يكون يتيم أبي طالب نبيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's favoring prophets indicates His favoring the Messenger; David's Psalms show Muhammad as final prophet and his community best, as 21:105 promises the earth to the righteous.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ولقد فضلنا بعض النبيين على بعض } إشارة إلى تفضيل رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite زبورا is allowed, or means some Psalms, or a passage about Muhammad named after the Psalms, like calling part of Qurʾān Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: قلت : يجوز أن يكون الزبور وزبور كالعباس وعباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are identified as angels, Jesus, Ezra, or jinn worshipped by Arabs who later accepted Islam unbeknown to them; none can remove or transfer harm.
rows.anchor: هم الملائكة ، وقيل : عيسى ابن مريم ، وعزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The beings invoked seek nearness to God through obedience and good works, hoping for mercy and fearing punishment; they are servants, not gods.
rows.anchor: أن آلهتهم أولئك يبتغون الوسيلة وهي القربة إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, أولئك is the subject, الذين يدعون its modifier, يبتغون its predicate; أيهم asks who is nearest or conveys striving to be nearest.
rows.anchor: مبتدأ ، و { الذين يدعون } صفته ، و { يبتغون } خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's punishment deserves caution from everyone, including a near angel or messenger.
rows.anchor: حقيقا بأن يحذره كل أحد من ملك مقرب ونبي مرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destruction means death or eradication; punishment means killing and other chastisement, with both recorded on the Preserved Tablet. One view assigns destruction to righteous towns and punishment to wicked ones.
rows.anchor: بالموت والاستئصال { أو معذبوها } بالقتل وأنواع العذاب

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil transmits predictions in al-Ḍaḥḥāk's books: Abyssinians destroy Mecca, famine strikes Medina, Basra floods, Turks enter Kufa, mountains face disasters, and Khurāsān faces varied trials.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل : وجدت في كتب الضحاك بن مزاحم في تفسيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording metaphorically says wisdom restrained sending signs; Quraysh demanded Ṣafā turned to gold or resurrection, but earlier peoples who rejected demanded signs were destroyed, so punishment for Muhammad's people was deferred.
rows.anchor: استعير المنع لترك إرسال الآيات من أجل صارف الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The she-camel of Ṣāliḥ was one such sign; its destruction was visible nearby to Arab travelers, yet its people rejected it. مبصرة means manifest and has a reading with fatḥa on mīm.
rows.anchor: وهي ناقة صالح ؛ لأن آثار هلاكهم في بلاد العرب قريبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If الآيات means demanded miracles, they warn of imminent destruction; if all signs, Qurʾān and other signs warn of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: إن أراد بها الآيات المقترحة فالمعنى لا نرسلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's encompassing the people means He announced victory over Quraysh at Badr as though it had happened, as in 54:45 and 3:12.
rows.anchor: واذكر إذ أوحينا إليك أن ربك أحاط بقريش

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Badr, in the shelter with Abū Bakr, the Prophet prayed for God's promise, then wore armor and encouraged the fighters with the prediction of defeat.
rows.anchor: وحين تزاحف الفريقان يوم بدر والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في العريش

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: At Badr's water the Prophet said he saw where the enemy would fall, pointing to each place; Quraysh heard what had been shown in his dream and mocked it.
rows.anchor: فقد كان يقول حين ورد ماء بدر ( والله لكأني أنظر إلى مصارع القوم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh mocked the prediction and the Tree of Zaqqum, reasoning fire burns stones but cannot nurture trees; the author answers God can create fire-resistant trees, as nature shows.
rows.anchor: فكانوا يضحكون ويستسخرون ويستعجلون به استهزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طينا is a circumstantial accusative either of the relative's object, meaning Adam's origin is clay, or of the relative clause, meaning he was clay when created.
rows.anchor: حال إما من الموصول والعامل فيه أسجد ، على : أأسجد له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أرأيتك means tell me about this; هاذا is its object, and Satan suppresses the question why Adam was favored before beginning his oath.
rows.anchor: الكاف للخطاب ، و { هاذا } مفعول به . والمعنى : أخبرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: لأحتنكن means to strip Adam's descendants bare through misguidance, like locusts consuming the earth; the author offers several explanations of Satan's inference and favors that he spoke before Adam ate.
rows.anchor: لأستأصلنهم بالإغواء ، من احتنك الجراد الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اذهب means abandonment, not literal travel, as in Moses' words to the Samaritan in 20:97; جزاؤكم shifts to plural for Satan and followers, and موفورا means fully paid.
rows.anchor: ليس من الذهاب الذي هو نقيض المجيء ، إنما معناه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: يا خيل الله اركبي exemplifies addressing mounted fighters as God's cavalry; الرجل is a collective noun for infantry and has readings.
rows.anchor: يا خيل الله اركبي . والرجل اسم جمع للراجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The voice, cavalry, and foot soldiers metaphorically depict Satan as a raider mobilizing an army; alternatively the voice calls to evil and troops are evildoers, perhaps literal forces.
rows.anchor: هو كلام ورد مورد التمثيل ، مثلت حاله في تسلطه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan shares wealth and children through sins such as usury, illicit earnings, pagan customs, immoral spending, withheld zakāt, illicit conception or false paternity, pagan names, and corrupting faith or conduct.
rows.anchor: وأما المشاركة في الأموال والأولاد فكل معصية يحملهم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His false promises include intercession, pride in lineage, delaying repentance, forgiveness without it, reliance on mercy or intercession, and preference for worldly gain.
rows.anchor: المواعيد الكاذبة . من شفاعة الآلهة والكرامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عبادي means the righteous, whom Satan cannot mislead; God suffices as their protector, as in the exception for His sincere servants.
rows.anchor: يريد الصالحين { ليس لك عليهم سلطان } أي لا تقدر أن تغويهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command to Satan is abandonment and withdrawal of protection, like telling sinners to do as they wish.
rows.anchor: هو من الأوامر الواردة على سبيل الخذلان والتخلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يزجي means setting ships moving; الضر means fear of drowning. At sea, other invocations disappear from thought and only God is remembered and trusted; alternatively, the false gods themselves cannot help.
rows.anchor: يجري ويسير . والضر : خوف الغرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative rebukes them, with an omitted premise: did you survive and then feel secure? جانب البر is the object of يخسف, with بكم circumstantial, meaning land collapses while they are upon it.
rows.anchor: الهمزة للإنكار ، والفاء للعطف على محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of the land's side shows all directions are equally under God's power: sinking on land is like drowning at sea. A ḥāṣib throws stones from above if they escape sinking below.
rows.anchor: الجوانب والجهات كلها في قدرته سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may return to sea through renewed need and be destroyed by a qāṣif, a crashing wind or one that breaks what it passes; readings vary between first- and second-person verb forms.
rows.anchor: أن يقوي دواعيكم ويوفر حوائجكم إلى أن ترجعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تبيعا means a claimant demanding redress, illustrated by al-Shammākh; none can exact vengeance from God. كفرتم means ingratitude for rescue.
rows.anchor: التبيع : المطالب ، من قوله { فاتباع بالمعروف }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Views of human honor include reason, speech, discernment, writing, fine appearance and stature, managing life, dominion over earthly things, or eating with fingers; al-Rashīd demonstrates this after Abū Yūsuf cites Ibn ʿAbbās.
rows.anchor: كرمه الله بالعقل ، والنطق ، والتمييز ، والخط ، والصورة الحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says كثير excludes angels, whose higher standing distinguishes them, and condemns the Mujabbira for claiming humans outrank angels and fabricating traditions for this view.
rows.anchor: هو ما سوى الملائكة وحسب بني آدم تفضيلا أن ترفع عليهم الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects a story in which angels request worldly pleasures and God promises the afterlife, as a fabricated report of human superiority.
rows.anchor: قالت الملائكة : ربنا إنك أعطيت بني آدم الدنيا يأكلون منها

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The author rejects as fabricated the attribution to Abū Hurayra that a believer is more honored to God than angels.
rows.anchor: ورووا عن أبي هريرة أنه قال : لمؤمن أكرم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects interpreting كثيرا as all created beings, which would prefer humans over angels; he calls this strained interpretation hostility to the heavenly assembly.
rows.anchor: بمعنى ( جميع ) في هذه الآية ، وخذلوا حتى سلبوا الذوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: يدعو has yāʾ or nūn readings, a passive reading, and a dialectal form from al-Ḥasan; the day phrase is accusative with implied اذكر or parsed as a plural marker.
rows.anchor: قرىء : ( يدعو ) ، بالياء والنون . ويدعى كل أناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بإمامهم means the prophet, religious leader, scripture, or religion followed, or the record of deeds; al-Ḥasan reads بكتابهم. The author ridicules the view it means mothers to honor Jesus, al-Ḥasan, and al-Ḥusayn, or hide illegitimate parentage.
rows.anchor: بمن ائتموا به من نبي أو مقدم في الدين ، أو كتاب ، أو دين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من takes plural agreement because it means a group. Both groups see their books, but the left-handed are too ashamed and tongue-tied to read effectively, while the right-handed read clearly and invite others.
rows.anchor: ولكن إذا اطلعوا على ما في كتابهم ، أخذهم ما يأخذ المطالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتيل means the smallest trace; the righteous lose no reward, as also stated in 19:60 and 20:112.
rows.anchor: ولا ينقصون من ثوابهم أدنى شيء ، كقوله { ولا يظلمون شيئا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blindness in this life means lacking guidance; the person is blind and further from the path in the Hereafter, where guidance no longer benefits them. Another analysis takes the second أعمى as comparative, explaining Abū ʿAmr's two readings.
rows.anchor: معناه : ومن كان في الدنيا أعمى ، فهو في الآخرة أعمى كذلك
